leads.name: National champion swamp tupelo
leads.note: American Forests reports it as national champion (337 points), 5-foot-thick trunk, 80 ft to first limb, 'growing on the bank of a small muddy creek deep in the heart of Congaree'. No trail, no coordinate, no public path found this pass. Needs a precise location before it could be a collectible point.

leads.name: National champion sweetgum
leads.note: 203in circumference, 160ft tall, near Cedar Creek in 'trackless, eastern wilderness', described as hidden by understory. No public trail access and no coordinate found; blocked-leaning rather than a lead, but keeping as a lead in case a trail or coordinate turns up.

leads.name: Former national champion laurel oak
leads.note: Reached only 'after a three-mile hike' per American Forests; no trail name or coordinate found this pass.

resolved.name: State champion bald cypress, east end of park
resolved.outcome: Verified and delivered as cgr_003, The General Greene Tree (Bates Ferry Trail, 30ft/914cm circumference), on 2026-09-26. Confirmed distinct from cgr_002 (Harry Hampton Tree, Oakridge Trail, 23'9"/724cm), which this lead had flagged as a possible duplicate; the two are different trails, different names and different circumferences. A separate, still-unresolved overlap is noted in cgr_003's own story: a Friends of Congaree essay's 'nearly 28ft' east-end champion figure may be an older measurement of this same tree or a genuine third giant.

resolved.name: Tallest loblolly pine on Weston Lake Loop near Bridge D
resolved.outcome: Verified and delivered as cgr_004, The Congaree National Champion Loblolly Pine (Weston Lake Loop near Bridge D, ~170ft/457cm circumference), on 2026-09-26. Confirmed distinct from cgr_001 (Richland County Pine, Boardwalk Loop, a FORMER state champion per NPS); this one is the current national champion per three independent sources.
